takeaway: Look at the whole picture, use what you have learned, and bring questions to your next clinical conversation.
why: Sleep, regular food, and hydration support your day alongside treatment and movement.

slides.title: One part of the picture
slides.content: Recovery is not about finding one perfect treatment. Movement, understanding, sleep, nourishment, hydration, and support each have a role. Which part needs attention will differ from person to person.

slides.title: Sleep and how you feel
slides.content: Pain can interrupt sleep. A difficult night can also leave you more tired, sensitive, or less able to cope the next day. That is a reason to support sleep—not a sign that one poor night has undone your recovery.

slides.title: Food supports the work
slides.content: Regular meals and enough food provide energy and nutrients for normal body function and activity. If you often miss meals, a practical starting point may be making one meal more reliable. Medical or dietary needs may require individual advice.

slides.title: Make hydration accessible
slides.content: Having a drink available with meals or during your usual breaks can make hydration easier to remember. Needs vary with health, activity, and weather. Follow any fluid guidance you have been given; more is not automatically better.

slides.title: Start with what fits
slides.content: You don't need to change everything at once. Pick one part of your routine that could use support: making time for sleep, preparing a meal, or keeping water nearby. Choose something realistic rather than a plan that adds more pressure.

slides.title: Build on it
slides.content: Ask yourself: what would make this easier to repeat? We will come back to these foundations in more detail. For now, keep moving within your plan and give yourself one manageable starting point.
